Internal: quick notes from the triage so far — attaching debug-snapshot-429s.log and a short mitigation plan.

Observations:
- Traffic spike at 08:44:50 PDT from a handful of Phoenix client IPs, sustained high connection churn.
- 429s originate at the edge rate limiter (we enforce per-tenant RPS but observed repeated bursts that exceed the soft window).
- Our metrics show a retry amplification pattern: ~3x increase in request volume driven by client-side retries (backoff not being honored); the SDKs appear to retry with short jitter after tokenization changes.
- Several worker pools hit high ephemeral memory usage which increased latencies and led to additional 5xxs/timeouts.

Immediate mitigation actions pushed (09:10):
1) Hard 100 RPS per-customer cap at the edge for Phoenix; this should stop amplification.
2) Disabled client-visible 429 passthrough for a subset of endpoints — returning a 503 with Retry-After to reduce client retry loops until SDK fix.
3) Rolling restart of two serving worker groups to clear memory fragmentation; prewarmed caches re-initialized.
4) Enabled the fallback lighter-weight model variant for Phoenix requests that exceed latency thresholds.

Expected impact: reduced request amplification within ~10–20 minutes, partial throughput restoration while we stabilize workers. Full restore depends on Phoenix SDK rollout; we estimate 60–90 minutes for a durable fix if client-side changes are needed.

Action items:
- Alex / Laura: confirm we can ask Phoenix to temporarily disable aggressive retry in their SDK and push a patch.
- Marissa / Sean: monitor error rates and confirm when 429s drop below baseline.
- Vivek: FYI — may need exec escalation for extended SLA impact.

Attachments: debug-snapshot-429s.log, mitigation-plan-v1.pdf

-Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: [Incident] Phoenix production — interim mitigation & ETA

Amira / Ethan —

Quick update from the on-call team: thanks for the request IDs, they helped us correlate the traffic. We’ve implemented a set of mitigations (summarized below) and are already seeing decreased amplification: 429 volume is down ~65% at the edge and timeouts are trending down.

What we did (already live):
- Enforced a hard 100 RPS per-tenant cap for Phoenix to stop retry storms at the edge.
- Returned 503 + Retry-After on aggressive endpoints so well-behaved clients back off.
- Rolled restarts on affected worker pools and prewarmed caches.
- Enabled a fallback smaller model variant for high latency requests to preserve throughput for critical requests.

Next steps / ETA:
- We expect error-rate and latency to materially improve in the next 20–30 minutes; we’ll post another update at 10:10 PDT.
- If improvement plateaus, we’ll temporarily route Phoenix traffic to a dedicated pool to guarantee capacity (this requires a 25–30 minute ops window).

We’re also tracking a follow-up action: coordinate an SDK patch to reduce retry aggressiveness and a joint RCA.

Status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/phoenix-20260512

Short term ask for Phoenix: if you can push a short SDK change to increase backoff or disable retries for 503/429s, that will help shorten the window. If you prefer, we can apply stricter edge throttling instead and follow with a dedicated routing plan.

—
Sean Gallagher
Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
